_notes: Williams/Bally Pinball 2000: a Cyrix MediaGX PC. PinMAME's .nv is the CMOS (0x30000 at
0x11000000), then the PLX EEPROM (0x80) and the clock (0x48).
The game OS keeps every setting, audit and high score in a CMOS record named by an 8-character
tag. The directory starts at 0x11002488: 24-byte entries { char tag[8]; u32 flags; u32 size;
u32 data address; u32 check }, until an entry of filler (0x33333333). Data is allocated downward
from 0x11020000 in the order the machine first needed it, so one tag sits at different
addresses on different machines: map fields name their record with 'tag', and their 'start' is
the offset inside the record. A reader resolves the tag first; a record the machine has not
created yet is not readable. The records' check words are not described here, so these maps
